title: Transport of a normalized left derived adjunction through exact equivalences
statement: Let A, B, A′, B′ be abelian categories with derived localizations in independent universes. Let e:A≃A′ and g:B≃B′ be additive equivalences. Let L⊣U and L′⊣U′ be additive adjunctions with exact right adjoints. Suppose natural isomorphisms Lg≅eL′ and Ue≅gU′ commute with the ordinary units. Given a universal left derived pair (LS,epsilonS) for L and an adjunction LS⊣D(U) whose unit followed by D(U)(epsilonS) and the fixed exact localization comparison equals the localized ordinary unit on every homotopy representative, there exist a universal left derived pair (LM,epsilonM) for L′ and an adjunction LM⊣D(U′), normalized by the ordinary L′⊣U′ unit. The derived left and right comparison isomorphisms D(e)LM≅LS D(g) and D(U)D(e)≅D(g)D(U′) satisfy respectively the counit and exact localization factorization identities specified in the Lean statement. They commute with the derived adjunction units on every object. This is transport of the universal pair and its normalized adjunction [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], without any exactness assumption on L or L′.

proof.text: Conjugate LS by D(e).inverse and D(g).functor. The two exact localization comparisons and the ordinary left square define the counit epsilonM. Transport the right Kan extension universal property through equivalences of its source, localized category and target. The equivalence unit supplies the derived left comparison and its counit factorization.

Localize the ordinary right square using the composition and natural-isomorphism APIs for exact derived functors. Their homotopy localization factorizations give the displayed right comparison formula.

Conjugate the source derived adjunction through the two derived equivalences, then transport its left and right functors by the two comparison isomorphisms. Equivalently use the invertible mate and full faithfulness of whiskering by an equivalence to adjust the right adjoint isomorphism. The mate-unit identity is the required unit square at every derived object.

Precompose the target unit-normalization equation with the source localization comparison. Naturality of the transported unit and the left counit factorization replace it by the source derived unit followed by the right comparison. Use naturality and the right localization factorization, then the source normalization. What remains is precisely the degreewise ordinary unit square, mapped to homotopy categories and localized. The source homotopy equivalence is essentially surjective, so naturality extends this equality to every target homotopy representative.

theorem normalizedDerivedAdjunctionTransport
    {A : Type a} {B : Type b} {A' : Type a'} {B' : Type b'}
    [Category.{av} A] [Category.{bv} B] [Category.{av'} A'] [Category.{bv'} B']
    [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [Abelian A'] [Abelian B']
    [HasDerivedCategory.{da} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{db} B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{da'} A'] [HasDerivedCategory.{db'} B']
    (e : A ≌ A') (g : B ≌ B') [e.functor.Additive] [e.inverse.Additive]
    [g.functor.Additive] [g.inverse.Additive]
    (L : A ⥤ B) (U : B ⥤ A) (L' : A' ⥤ B') (U' : B' ⥤ A')
    [L.Additive] [U.Additive] [L'.Additive] [U'.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits U] [PreservesFiniteColimits U]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits U'] [PreservesFiniteColimits U']
    (a : L ⊣ U) (a' : L' ⊣ U')
    (s : L ⋙ g.functor ≅ e.functor ⋙ L')
    (r : U ⋙ e.functor ≅ g.functor ⋙ U')
    (hu : ∀ X : A, e.functor.map (a.unit.app X) ≫ r.hom.app (L.obj X) ≫
      U'.map (s.hom.app X) = a'.unit.app (e.functor.obj X))
    (LS : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (εS : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ LS ⟶ L.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    (hLS : LS.IsLeftDerivedFunctor εS (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ)))
    (aS : LS ⊣ U.mapDerivedCategory)
    (hn : ∀ H : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ),
      aS.unit.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj H) ≫ U.mapDerivedCategory.map (εS.app H) ≫
        U.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app ((L.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj H) =
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map ((a.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).unit.app H)) :
    let DR := e.mapDerivedCategory
    let DS := g.mapDerivedCategory
    let kR := e.functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh
    let kS := g.functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh
    let sH := Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso s (.up ℤ) ≪≫
      (Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso (Iso.refl (e.functor ⋙ L')) (.up ℤ)).symm
    let rH := Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso r (.up ℤ) ≪≫
      (Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso (Iso.refl (g.functor ⋙ U')) (.up ℤ)).symm
    ∃ (LM : DerivedCategory A' ⥤ DerivedCategory B')
      (εM : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ LM ⟶ L'.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
      (c : DR.functor ⋙ LM ≅ LS ⋙ DS.functor)
      (d : U.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ DR.functor ≅ DS.functor ⋙ U'.mapDerivedCategory)
      (aM : LM ⊣ U'.mapDerivedCategory),
      LM.IsLeftDerivedFunctor εM (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A' (.up ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ H : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ),
        LM.map (kR.hom.app H) ≫ εM.app ((e.functor.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj H) =
          c.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj H) ≫ DS.functor.map (εS.app H) ≫
            kS.hom.app ((L.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj H) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Qh.map (sH.hom.app H)) ∧
      (∀ H : HomotopyCategory B (.up ℤ),
        d.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj H) =
          DR.functor.map (U.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app H) ≫
            kR.hom.app ((U.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj H) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Qh.map (rH.hom.app H) ≫
            U'.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv.app
              ((g.functor.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj H) ≫
            U'.mapDerivedCategory.map (kS.inv.app H)) ∧
      (∀ H : HomotopyCategory A' (.up ℤ),
        aM.unit.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj H) ≫ U'.mapDerivedCategory.map (εM.app H) ≫
          U'.mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app ((L'.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj H) =
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map ((a'.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).unit.app H)) ∧
      (∀ K : DerivedCategory A,
        DR.functor.map (aS.unit.app K) ≫ d.hom.app (LS.obj K) =
          aM.unit.app (DR.functor.obj K) ≫ U'.mapDerivedCategory.map (c.hom.app K))
